validity.researcher_notes: SPEC (diameter) is materially wrong. GEM lists Diameter=24 in for the Rumaila->Nasiriyah gas pipeline. The row's OWN sole gem.wiki citation is a generic OPEC Annual Statistics Bulletin 2012 (p.75) — an aggregate national pipeline-length table that does NOT name this pipeline or give a diameter, so it supports neither 24 in nor the row's existence. The best independent source found, the Dhi Qar (Nasiriyah) CCGT Power Plant ESIA (Sept 2018, hosted by the US DFC), states plainly: 'Natural gas required for the Power Plant will be supplied from the North Rumila national 42-inch pipeline through an interconnection pipeline of about 70 m length to be constructed by the Ministry of Oil.' i.e. the national gas trunk reaching Nasiriyah from North Rumaila is 42-inch, not 24-inch. This is reinforced by internal inconsistency in GEM's own numbers: Capacity=10.42 bcm/y (~1 bcf/d) is implausible for a 24-inch line (cf. GEM's own P1850 Khor Al-Zubair-Hartha 24 in = 4.80 bcm/y) but is consistent with a 42-inch trunk (cf. GEM P2234 North Rumela-Khor Al-Zubair 42 in = 10.00 bcm/y; P1852 Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha 42 in = 11.03 bcm/y). Weight of evidence => diameter should be 42 in. Length (216 km) is geographically plausible for Rumaila->Nasiriyah (~180-220 km) but I found NO independent numeric confirmation of 216 km; Capacity 10.42 bcm/y likewise has no independent numeric confirmation — both left UNRESOLVED, not filled. url_verifier returns OK/200 for the ESIA URL (not blocklisted) but cannot parse PDF text streams, so its token check false-negatives; I confirmed the '42-inch'/'North Rumila'/'Nasiriyah'/'Safwan-Zubair DGS-Tuba-Rumaila-Nasiriyah' tokens locally via pdftotext of the same 200 response.

validity.recommendation: Keep the row (real, correctly classified gas trunk) but (a) apply the 42-in diameter fix above, (b) reconcile segment boundaries/diameters against P1852 (Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha, 42 in, 470 km, also ending at Nasiriyah) and the under-construction 'North Rumela-Al-Najaf Gas Pipeline' — these three GEM entries appear to describe one physical 42-in North Rumaila->Nasiriyah->north national trunk and may double-count segments.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED as a real national gas trunk, not a phantom. The Dhi Qar CCGT ESIA independently establishes a natural-gas pipeline delivering North Rumaila gas to the Nasiriyah power complex, with a named corridor 'Safwan-Zubair DGS-Tuba-Rumaila-Nasiriyah-Strategy Road-Al Kidhir-Batha'. CLASSIFICATION: CONFIRMED correct — it is a gas transmission trunk (dry gas to the national grid / power stations), not an oil/NGL line and not a gathering/process line; none of the GulfPub Iraq oil lines match this route (no crude line runs Rumaila->Nasiriyah). ATTRIBUTION: CONFIRMED — the ESIA states the pipeline belongs to the Ministry of Oil / Oil Pipelines Company ('the necessary site surveys ... have been completed and the Oil Pipelines Company is committed to proceed', and 'fuel pipelines belong to the Government of Iraq'), matching GEM Owner=Iraq Ministry of Oil 100%; FuelSource=Rumaila (North Rumaila) and StartProvince=Basrah / EndProvince=Dhi Qar are all corroborated. Status=operating is supported: the ESIA treats the North Rumaila 42-in 'national' pipeline as an existing line to be tapped. DUPLICATE CAVEAT (not opened as a hard concern): the ESIA corridor shows one 42-in trunk running North Rumaila -> Nasiriyah -> onward along the 'Strategy Road', which is the same physical alignment plausibly represented by P1852 (Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha, 42 in) and the under-construction North Rumela-Al-Najaf line. P1851 as the discrete Rumaila->Nasiriyah southern segment is defensible, but Baird should verify the segmentation is not a double-count and that diameters are consistent (all 42 in) across these rows.

routes.corridor_desc: North Rumaila 42-inch national gas trunk running NW from the North Rumaila field gas hub (Basra) to the Nasiriyah power complex (Dhi Qar), roughly along the Basra-Nasiriyah 'Strategy Road' (the strategic-pipeline highway corridor). The Dhi Qar CCGT ESIA names the corridor 'Safwan-Zubair DGS-Tuba-Rumaila-Nasiriyah-Strategy Road-Al Kidhir-Batha', which places the southern gas source at the Zubair/Rumaila degassing stations and the delivery point at Nasiriyah, continuing north beyond Nasiriyah along the Strategy Road toward Al Khidhir/Batha. Endpoints are firmly named; the exact pipeline alignment between them is NOT surveyed here, so the corridor is bounded loosely to the ~180-220 km Basra->Nasiriyah axis (consistent with the 216 km GEM length). Coordinates are approximate, derived from the named places' locations, NOT from a sourced pipeline vertex; no coordinate was invented.
